title: Proactive GPU Warm-pool Federation and Cost Throttler
author: Maya Chen
body:
Summary:
This page describes the design, Terraform module usage, CI/CD rollout, operational runbook, and alerting for the Proactive GPU Warm-pool Federation and Cost Throttler (PGW-C). PGW-C is a multi-account, multi-region warm-pool coordination layer plus a cost-aware admission controller that: 
- Keeps preloaded model KV caches and warmed containers on a curated set of GPU nodes.
- Federates warm capacity across regional pools with fair-share and reclaim policies.
- Enforces cost throttling and burst protection to meet monthly committed capacity budgets.

Goals:
- Reduce cold-starts for inference by maintaining a warmed pool of model-serving sessions.
- Provide predictable unit economics by limiting uncontrolled burst usage and applying fair-share.
- Enable safe, incremental rollouts of warm-pool policies via CI/CD and Terraform.

Scope:
- Applies to hosted and dedicated clusters managed by eng-infra (gpu clusters tagged: redwood:gpubackend).
- Covers on-demand, spot, and dedicated pre-warm nodes.
- Integrates with: gpu-warm-manager, pool-orchestrator, spot-fallback-allocator, warm-pool-metrics-exporter, account-billing-sidecar.

Architecture Overview:
- gpu-warm-manager (Kubernetes deployment per region): watches model manifests, reconciles warm sessions, and executes seeding jobs to load KV cache into serving runtime.
- pool-orchestrator (central control plane service): maintains global view of warm-pool capacity, enforces federation policies, computes cross-region rebalancing ops, signals terraform operator for provisioning.
- cost-throttler (admission controller): webhook that inspects incoming infer requests and applies throttles or fallback model variants when cost budgets are exceeded.
- metrics pipeline: warm-pool-metrics-exporter -> prometheus -> cortex long-term store.

Key Metrics and SLOs:
- Warm-hit-rate (fraction of requests served from warmed sessions): target >= 95% (prod); warning >= 92%.
- Cold-start-rate (requests that triggered a cold session): target <= 5% per hour window.
- Average rewarm latency (time to seed a KV cache on a node): target <= 18s (95th percentile).
- Budget overspend incidents (cost from burst above committed budget): target 0 per month; alert on > 1% over commitment for 24h.

Federation & Fair-share Policies (summary):
- Pools are grouped by tenant priority (tiers: enterprise, plat, self-serve).
- Each pool advertises: available-warm-sessions, preemptible-capacity, cost-rate-per-token.
- Orchestrator computes fair-share allocation every 60s and emits transfer proposals.
- Transfer proposals are gated by safety checks (latency impact, network egress threshold, cross-account policy).

Terraform modules and variables (example):
- Module path: terraform/modules/gpu-warm-pool
- Important variables:
  - name (string)
  - region (string)
  - account_id (string)
  - desired_warm_sessions (number)
  - spot_fallback_ratio (number, default 0.25)
  - budget_monthly_usd (string)

Terraform snippet (example usage):
```
module "eu-warmpool" {
  source = "../modules/gpu-warm-pool"
  name   = "eu-prod-warmpool"
  region = "eu-west-1"
  account_id = "123456789012"
  desired_warm_sessions = 120
  spot_fallback_ratio = 0.2
  budget_monthly_usd = "15000"
}
```

CI/CD and Rollout Strategy:
1) Feature branch: create terraform/pgw changes and a small canary for gpu-warm-manager (2 nodes) in staging.
2) Integration tests: automated smoke that verifies warm-hit-rate improves vs baseline and that cost-throttler correctly gates tokens.
3) Canary promotion: promote to 10% of traffic in prod region; observe for 72 hours.
4) Gradual ramp: expand to 30% then 60% over successive days if no regressions.
5) Full promotion: apply Terraform to all configured regions and mark the module as promoted in the iac registry.

Rollback criteria (automated gates):
- Warm-hit-rate drop > 2% from pre-rollout baseline for 30m.
- Error-rate increase > 1% (absolute) or latency P95 increase > 150ms.
- Cost anomalies: projected monthly overrun > 3% on daily extrapolation.

Operational Runbook (Incident Triage):
1) Detection:
  - Alerts: warm-hit-rate < 92% (critical), cold-start-rate > 8% (critical), cost-overspend-warning (high).
  - Dashboards: per-region warm session inventory, cross-account transfer queue, admission-blocked-requests.
2) Initial mitigation:
  - If warm-hit-rate low: execute `kubectl -n redwood scale deployment/gpu-warm-manager --replicas=3` to force additional seeding.
  - If cold-start storm: enable emergency soft-throttle: POST /v1/admin/throttle?policy=soft-burst to cost-throttler.
  - If cross-region egress threshold tripped: pause federation by toggling orchestrator flag: `kubectl set env deployment/pool-orchestrator ENABLE_FEDERATION=false`.
3) Reconciliation steps:
  - Run `pgwctl rebuild --region eu-west-1 --models popular-models` to re-seed top-20 models.
  - Inspect Prometheus query: `sum(rate(warm_pool_seed_errors_total[5m])) by (region)` and remediate pod logs.
4) Post-incident:
  - Create a postmortem within 48 hours. Record state changes and terraform diffs.
  - Adjust warm_session targets or bump budget; add preflight checks in CI if needed.

Prometheus Alerts (examples):
- Alert: PGW_WarmHitRateLow
  Expression: `warm_hit_rate{env="prod"} < 0.92`
  For: 10m
  Severity: critical
  Runbook: Follow Operational Runbook above.

- Alert: PGW_BudgetOverspendForecast
  Expression: `increase(cost_throttler_spend_usd_total[24h]) / (budget_monthly_usd / 30) > 1.01`
  For: 6h
  Severity: high
  Runbook: Throttle non-enterprise tiers and open a billing incident.

Cost Throttler Config (table):
| key | description | example |
|------|-------------|---------|
| global_burst_limit | Max sessions above target across all pools | 150 |
| tenant_min_reserve | Minimum sessions reserved per tier | enterprise: 30, plat: 10 |
| burst_window_seconds | Sliding window for burst accounting | 3600 |
| overspend_action | Action on projected overspend | soft_throttle | 

Admission Control behaviors:
- soft_throttle: queue requests up to 30s and return token cost hints to clients.
- hard_reject: immediate 429 with recommended fallback model id.
- fallback_model: map of compatible lower-cost model variants per tenant.

Safety and Security Considerations:
- Account boundaries: cross-account federation writes are implemented using provisioning roles with least privilege policies; terraform operator uses temporary STS tokens.
- KMS: all model seeds are performed with ephemeral keys; KMS key usage logged in audit-logging service.
- Data residency: federation respects region-specific residency flags; orchestrator rejects proposals that violate residency.

Operational Playbooks and Commands (cheat-sheet):
- Check warm inventory: `pgwctl inventory --region us-west-2`
- Force re-seed model list: `pgwctl rebuild --models "gpt-small,gpt-embed" --parallel 8`
- Pause federation: `kubectl set env deployment/pool-orchestrator ENABLE_FEDERATION=false -n redwood`
- Unblock cost-throttler: `curl -X POST https://admin.internal/cost-throttler/unblock --header "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN"`

Testing Guidance for Eng Teams:
- Local run: run `make dev-warm-manager` to start a single-node warm-manager and exercise seeding flows against a local runtime.
- CI testcases to include: 
  - Warm session reconciliation under flapping node conditions.
  - Cross-account transfer approval/denial flows.
  - Cost-throttler behavior under synthetic overspend.

Ownership and Contacts:
- Primary owner: eng-infra/gpu-capacity team (oncall: gpu-capacity-oncall@redwood.internal)
- Pager: #infra-oncall (Slack)
- Escalation: Head of Eng Infra (Arjun Patel) -> CTO on-call if incident > 4h.

References and Links:

- internal runbooks: /confluence/eng-infra/runbooks/kv-cache-consensus-and-warmup-coordination-runbook.json
- observability dashboards: grafana/redwood/pgw-overview

Change Log:
- 2024-11-05: Document created by Maya Chen.
- 2024-12-10: Added cost-throttler policies and Prometheus alerts (review by Arjun).
- 2025-01-18: Updated SLO targets and rollback criteria; added federation pause command.

Appendix: Sample alert playbook checklist (to attach to pager duty incidents)
1) Acknowledge incident in PagerDuty.
2) Run `pgwctl inventory` and capture top 5 models by cold-start count.
3) If warm-hit-rate trending down, scale warm-manager and trigger re-seed for top models.
4) If cost forecast > 2% overspend, enable tiered soft-throttle and notify billing.
5) Attach terraform plan and recent CI job ids to the incident ticket.

Note: This document is intended to be a living playbook. Engineers should update the Terraform module references and CI job names when promoting changes.
